title: Youth Suicide in Japan: Exploring the Role of Subcultures, Internet Addiction, and Societal Pressures
content: Background: Youth suicide in Japan remains a significant societal issue, driven by a complex combination of academic pressures, social isolation, bullying, and family issues. In recent years, internet addiction and the influence of subcultures have increasingly played a role in shaping the psychological landscape of young people. The COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated these challenges, intensifying feelings of loneliness and anxiety about the future. This study explores how internet addiction, gaming culture, and Japan’s unique subcultures contribute to the risk of youth suicide. Methods: This paper reviews existing literature and statistical data on youth suicide in Japan, examining the influence of internet addiction and subcultures on suicide risk. It also compares suicide rates in Japan with those in other developed countries and analyzes the impact of societal pressures on youth suicide. The study further investigates how these factors interact with the mental health crisis exacerbated by the pandemic. Results: In 2023, 513 school-aged youth died by suicide, maintaining a disturbingly high rate. Key risk factors identified include academic pressure, bullying (particularly cyberbullying), family issues, and internet addiction. The influence of subcultures, including anime, manga, and gaming, plays a significant role in the emotional struggles faced by youth, contributing to feelings of alienation and despair. The COVID-19 pandemic worsened social isolation, mental health issues, and suicide rates among youth, with significant long-term psychological effects. Conclusions: The study highlights the urgent need for comprehensive mental health support systems in Japan, including better access to counseling services in schools and communities. Addressing cultural attitudes toward mental health, regulating harmful online content, and understanding the impact of subcultures on youth are essential for preventing suicide. Family-based interventions and broader societal efforts are crucial for creating a supportive environment that can help reduce suicide rates among young people.
